mutants.reason: The PSLVERR clear in the RESP state is inverted. PSLVERR is then not cleared after the PREADY cycle, so an error stays high while PREADY is low.
With HS_TYPE=1 the launch no longer raises the request bit (it stays 0). The four-phase handshake never starts, so no completer transfer and no PREADY occur.
The PSLVERR clear condition is inverted (state != RESP). The error stays high through the PREADY cycle and is cleared in the other states, so PSLVERR is not limited to the PREADY cycle.

This line sits in the VLSIT_SYNTHESIS branch for CELL_TYPE=2. With RST_VAL=0 the inverted condition selects the SN cell, so the synchronizer resets to 1. After reset the request event is spurious and a transfer starts with no Setup. It is invisible in the simulation build only because the line is not compiled there.
With APB5=1 the mst wake-up register is forced to 0, so a synchronized i_apb_pwakeup never reaches o_apb_pwakeup. With APB5=0 the slv gate hides the difference.
The HS_TYPE condition is swapped. Two-phase sets the acknowledge to 1 instead of toggling it, so the second transfer never sees an acknowledge event. Four-phase would toggle instead.
With HS_TYPE=1 the acknowledge is never raised at the end of the transfer. The mst side waits forever and PREADY never comes.
In the delayed-update path (sim_extra != 0) the pending flag is not set. The delayed value is never applied, so a crossing with extra latency never arrives.
The two-phase request event polarity is inverted (equal instead of different). A transfer starts in idle with no Setup and the real request is missed.

At sim_cnt==0 sim_cur takes sim_nxt and pend should clear. With pend left at 1 the model just re-assigns sim_cur <= sim_nxt, which already holds that value. Any input change overwrites pend and sim_nxt in the change branch. The output sequence never differs.
The simulation bypass condition is inverted. Types 1 to 4 become a zero-stage bypass with no synchronizer latency, and type 0 gets a metastability chain.
The sense of +APBCDC_MSYNC_EN is inverted. With EN=0 the random extra latency is applied, so the CHK-025 duration bound (model off) can be exceeded.

This line is inside the branch LPARA_UREQ_W != 0, so APB5=1 and USER_REQ_W != 0. Then LPARA_PUREQ_W equals USER_REQ_W and the padding width is 0. The replicated 1'b1 contributes no bits, so the port value is the same.
The wake-up register resets to 1. With APB5=1 a spurious wake-up crosses to o_apb_pwakeup while idle after reset release, and during a staggered reset release.
The reset condition of the slv payload register is inverted. It is cleared while running and loaded in reset, so the request fields are not 0 in reset and are lost in operation.
The reset condition of the mst response register is inverted. PRDATA and PSLVERR are not reset and the response is lost during normal operation.
The HS_TYPE condition of the request launch is swapped. Two-phase raises the request instead of toggling it, and four-phase toggles.

This line sits in the VLSIT_SYNTHESIS branch for CELL_TYPE=3. With RST_VAL=0 the SN cell is chosen, so the synchronizer resets to 1 and a spurious request event follows reset release. It is invisible in the simulation build only because the line is not compiled there.
The condition that clears the four-phase request is inverted. In four-phase the request is never dropped. In two-phase it is cleared spuriously, which breaks the toggle.
The PENABLE condition is inverted, so PENABLE is high outside ACCESS and low in the Access phase.

The default simulation model is disabled when no plusarg is given. The random extra crossing latency (0 to 2 cycles) is no longer applied, so output timing changes. The latency stays within the windows, so no requirement is violated.
With sim_extra==0 the pending flag is set to 1 instead of 0. The next cycle then loads a stale or X sim_nxt into sim_cur and corrupts the crossed bit.

This line sits in the VLSIT_SYNTHESIS branch for CELL_TYPE=4. The inverted condition picks the SN cell, so the synchronizer resets to 1 and a spurious request event follows reset release. It is invisible in the simulation build only because the line is not compiled there.
o_apb_penable resets to 1. During reset the output is high without PSEL.
The request bit resets to 1. The two-phase request and acknowledge are unequal after reset, so the slv side sees a spurious request and starts a transfer with no Setup.
The PREADY condition in ACCESS is inverted. The transfer ends when PREADY is low and waits while it is high.
The launch condition is inverted. The request bit changes when there is no Setup and is not toggled on a real Setup, so transfers are lost or spurious.
The two-phase acknowledge event polarity is inverted. The mst side sees the acknowledge immediately or never, so PREADY comes at the wrong time or not at all.

This line sits in the synthesis branch. The bypass condition is inverted, so types 1 to 4 become a plain wire with no synchronizer stage and type 0 gets the 4-FF cell. The crossing latency windows are violated. It is invisible in the simulation build only because the line is not compiled there.
The HS_TYPE condition of the request event is swapped. Two-phase uses the level form and four-phase the toggle form, so the handshake breaks.
The wake-up in-progress term is inverted. With APB5=1 and no i_apb_pwakeup, o_apb_pwakeup is high in idle and low during the Access phase while o_apb_psel is high.
The model resets the pending flag to 1 instead of 0. After reset release a stale or X sim_nxt is loaded into sim_cur, so X or a wrong value appears on the crossed bit.
The sim_extra==0 test is inverted. A zero extra delay is treated as pending and a nonzero one is applied immediately, so the crossed bit is wrong or X.

This line is inside the branch LPARA_UDAT_W != 0, so APB5=1 and USER_DATA_W != 0. Then LPARA_PUDAT_W equals USER_DATA_W and the padding width is 0. The replicated 1'b1 contributes no bits, so the port value is the same.
